page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the average tier for general-purpose workloads. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2691.89. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the average range. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 514.76 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 45.33 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 27.85 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution for tasks such as static web serving, software compilation, and database operations. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, medium-traffic web servers, and light development environments.
